objective.rule: A candidate is never VALIDATED from documentation or a tiny probe alone. It becomes VALIDATED only after a live small availability probe plus a representative full-fragment write -> read -> reassembly -> exact-length -> SHA-256 round-trip using the same chunking rules as code replication.

hard_gates: HTTPS public endpoint only; reject private/local networks and credential-bearing URLs.

No user-supplied credentials, manual authorization or permanent API secret required for the autonomous path. A provider-issued ephemeral anonymous token is allowed only when it is created programmatically from an officially documented unauthenticated endpoint and is not needed for public reads.
Free use and automation must be explicitly documented or otherwise clearly permitted; never infer permission from technical reachability.
Synthetic probe only. Never upload user memory during qualification.
Round-trip must preserve the exact original bytes after the adapter decoder.

Representative-load gate is mandatory before VALIDATED: test at least the current real code-shard size (or the configured safety floor), write every chunk through the actual adapter, read every chunk back, reassemble, compare exact length and SHA-256. Cached proof is reusable only while fresh and only for payloads no larger than the proven representative size.
Persist the provider-returned read locator in the shard manifest when upload and read URLs differ.
A fixed retention target must be >= 90 days. A renewable target is a distinct model and is eligible only after renewal behavior is documented and a live renewal proof succeeds.
On 4xx/5xx, content mismatch, redirect anomaly, policy change, expiry regression or repeated timeout: quarantine the target and continue searching instead of retrying the same candidate forever.
Revalidate selected providers periodically and immediately replace a target that no longer passes.

fixed.eligible_when: documented days >= minimum retention and live round-trip succeeds

declared_never.eligible_when: provider offers 'never' or equivalent, live round-trip succeeds, and MEL still revalidates because 'never' is not a service warranty

renewable.eligible_when: provider documents that a permitted access renews retention, MEL proves the renewal mechanism, and refresh cadence leaves a safety margin; ordinary status checks do not count unless documentation says they do

failure_memory.reason: Live write/read worked, but documented retention is below MEL's 90-day durability gate.
failure_memory.lesson: A successful round-trip does not override insufficient retention.

failure_memory.reason: Retention is short and recent round-trip behavior was not reliable enough.
failure_memory.lesson: Fast anonymous upload is not equivalent to durable storage.

failure_memory.reason: Durability is attractive on paper, but MEL's latest real infrastructure probe returned HTTP 412.
failure_memory.lesson: Documentation never overrides a failed live probe from the deployment environment.

failure_memory.reason: Guest retention is about 10 days, below the durability gate.
failure_memory.lesson: Guest and account retention must not be conflated.

failure_memory.reason: Free files expire after 60 days of inactivity; provider explicitly discourages using the free plan as long-term backup storage.
failure_memory.lesson: Do not turn a public-sharing free tier into backup storage against the provider's stated intent.

failure_memory.reason: Free expiry begins at 15 days and extends only through repeated downloads, capped at 45 days.
failure_memory.lesson: Do not manufacture artificial downloads just to simulate durability.

failure_memory.reason: Live Cloudflare probe returned HTTP 403 even though the public agent API is documented.
failure_memory.lesson: A provider can be suitable in a browser or another agent environment and still reject the deployed Worker; keep infrastructure-specific live proof mandatory.

failure_memory.reason: After switching to the provider's direct-download representation, MEL's deployed preview completed write/read/exact-byte comparison.
failure_memory.lesson: When an upload API returns a presentation URL, prefer the provider's explicit direct-download form for integrity probes.

candidate_targets.name: Pastebin.ai
candidate_targets.notes: Anonymous POST /api/v1/pastes is documented; reasonable API automation is permitted within limits. Use unlisted plaintext containing base64url of the encrypted shard and save raw_url.

candidate_targets.name: dpaste.com
candidate_targets.notes: Anonymous create is available; automated clients should send User-Agent and stay <= 1 request/s. Save returned Location and fetch its raw .txt representation.

candidate_targets.name: PasteMyst
candidate_targets.notes: Open/free API with anonymous operations and explicit never/1y expiry choices. Use current API generation and verify response schema before activation.

candidate_targets.name: 1C3
candidate_targets.notes: Anonymous text/file upload, 50 MB max, 1h-365d expiry. Stay far below published rate limits and never perform mass uploads.

candidate_targets.name: paste.c-net.org
candidate_targets.notes: Console-friendly binary paste service; documentation/community references describe 180-day expiry reset by access. MEL must still verify TLS/DNS and round-trip from its own infrastructure.

candidate_targets.name: MSK Paste
candidate_targets.notes: Documented public JSON API with no authentication, 1 MB content and 1y expiry. Create rate limit is documented; respect Retry-After.

candidate_targets.name: FileDitch
candidate_targets.notes: Scripts/bots are explicitly supported. Files have no scheduled expiry while accessed; only files untouched 45+ days may be removed when space is needed. Status API checks do not renew the clock, so MEL must not mistake HEAD/status for a retention refresh.

candidate_targets.name: Telegraph
candidate_targets.notes: createAccount is unauthenticated and returns the short-lived/use-scoped access token MEL needs to create a public page; reads are public and require no token. Never ask the user for credentials.

scoring_principles: Prefer independent operators/providers before adding a second endpoint from the same operator.
Latency can break ties but must never compensate for retention, policy or integrity failure.
Confidence increases only from current evidence and repeated successful probes; age reduces confidence.

operational_use.rule: Never write a real shard to an endpoint that is not currently VALIDATED. Use selected targets returned by the live discovery engine, persist the provider-returned remote locator, and always verify the stored bytes on read.
write_flow: Take the already encrypted ShardVault shard bytes.
Select a currently VALIDATED external endpoint, preferring operator diversity and avoiding a provider already holding too many fragments.
Apply the endpoint adapter exactly: raw binary only where documented; otherwise encode encrypted bytes as base64url or RFC4648 base64 according to that adapter.
Perform the documented anonymous write. If the provider returns an id, Location, raw_url or public URL, persist that returned locator in the shard descriptor instead of reconstructing it later.
Immediately read the object back using the provider-specific read representation.
Decode adapter wrapping and compare exact length plus every byte against the encrypted shard.
Only after exact match mark that fragment stored. On mismatch, 4xx/5xx, unexpected redirect or missing locator: quarantine that endpoint for the cycle and use another validated target.
read_flow: Read from the manifest's persisted remote locator, not from a guessed URL.
Use the adapter-specific direct/raw representation where available.
Decode base64/base64url wrapping only after a successful HTTP read.
Verify cryptographic/integrity expectations before reconstructing the vault data.
If a target fails, continue with redundant fragments and schedule revalidation/replacement.
maintenance: Re-run live probes periodically and after any provider error burst.
Keep seven or more independent validated external targets when possible.
Replace failed targets; never lower retention or integrity gates just to keep the count at seven.
Keep R2/D1 internal fallbacks separate from external diversity.
Revalidate the representative full-fragment proof when it expires or when MEL's required code-shard size increases.
A target with only a historical small probe may remain visible for diagnostics but must not count toward the validated 7-code-target goal.

discovery_method.goal: Find new zero-cost, automation-compatible, public-read storage/paste/file APIs that can be used without user-supplied credentials and can satisfy the durability gate.
search_cycle: Generate several materially different search queries instead of repeating one phrase.
Search official documentation, current public API catalogs, GitHub repositories, self-hostable projects with public instances, and provider terms/help pages.
Extract candidate host, write method, request content type, auth model, response locator, raw/direct read method, size limit, expiry/retention, rate limits, and automation policy.
Reject immediately if user login, payment, private-network access, permanent user API key, prohibited automation, or retention below the gate is required.
For provider-issued anonymous tokens, verify the token can be created programmatically from an unauthenticated documented endpoint and that public reads need no user secret.
Translate documentation into a bounded adapter profile: write method+URL, payload transform, form/JSON field names, response locator extraction, read URL, read transform, timeout and retention model.
Persist failures and rejection reasons so the next cycle changes query/provider family instead of retrying the same dead target forever.
Run a small synthetic availability probe from MEL's deployed Cloudflare environment to reject dead or blocked endpoints cheaply.

For every candidate that could be promoted, run a representative proof using the current real code-shard size (minimum safety floor when code size is unavailable) and the exact runtime chunking rules.
The representative proof must write all chunks, read all chunks, reassemble them, compare exact byte length, and match SHA-256 before the target can become VALIDATED.
Persist representative_bytes, representative_sha256, representative_parts and representative_verified_at. Re-run the proof when it expires or when the required fragment grows beyond the proven size.
Only after retention evidence plus small-probe success plus representative proof may the target enter VALIDATED/selected sets.

adapter_patterns: JSON text API: encode encrypted bytes as base64url and extract id/raw_url from JSON.
Form paste API: URL-encode or multipart the base64url text and save returned Location/public URL.
Multipart file API: upload a harmless .txt wrapper containing base64url unless binary is explicitly accepted.
Raw binary API: send application/octet-stream only when documentation and live probe confirm it.
Ephemeral anonymous-token API: create a provider-issued anonymous token first, use it only for creation, and persist only the public read locator unless later writes require the token.
Presentation URL providers: prefer documented raw/direct-download representation for integrity reads.
discovery_method.stop_condition: Stop expanding only when at least seven independent targets are live-validated; continue periodic discovery afterward for replacements and diversity.
